overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by listing "Election of City Clerk" on the June 15, 2026 notice without the candidate's name; the public hearing notice claim was rejected.

allegations.summary: Notice for a public hearing on a utility petition described a pole relocation, but the utility said at the meeting it would install a new pole instead.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice was sufficient where the Council only anticipated discussion of a pole relocation and was not aware that National Grid intended to install a new pole until the day of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Notice topic 'Election of City Clerk' did not name the candidate the Council appointed at the June 15, 2026 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the topic, “Election of City Clerk,” was insufficiently specific where it did not list the name of the applicant to be considered and appointed.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that a finding of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
